01

The questions practitioners are answering first

Where practice runs ahead

Each bubble is a topic cluster from the topic network, with the share of its recorded positions that come from spoken sources, and what that cluster is doing over time. The pattern is the point: the clusters where practitioners dominate are overwhelmingly the rising ones. Matter Workflows and Human Orchestration are the two fastest-growing clusters in the whole corpus, and both are more than half practitioner testimony. Select a bubble to read only that cluster — or use the ranked list in section 02, which filters the same way.

What it is built from+

Second Chair is this project’s evidence base: 600 works on AI and the legal profession, 1953–2026 — scholarship, industry evidence, court materials and practitioner interviews — each read end to end. The Analysis section applies two published analytical lenses: topic mapping and actor mapping, with driver and dynamics mapping and scenario mapping in progress.

03

Four different kinds of thing to say

Statement types

This is a distinction about the statement, not the speaker. A vendor's account of their own review process is the best evidence anywhere about that process; the same vendor's projection about 2030 is a different kind of claim entirely. Tagging them apart is what makes it possible to use practitioner testimony as primary evidence without either discounting it or over-reading it.
